title: isn't, haven't, don't etc. (negatives)
subtitle: I'm not / it isn't / I didn't
summary: Make negative sentences with not (n't) after am/is/have/will/can etc., and with don't, doesn't or didn't for other verbs.

lesson.heading: am not / isn't / wasn't
lesson.text: We put **not** (**n't**) after am, is, are, was and were.

lesson.heading: haven't / won't / can't / shouldn't
lesson.text: We do the same with have, has, will, can, could, must, should and would.

lesson.heading: don't / doesn't / didn't
lesson.note: **do**/**does** is the present, **did** is the past. The verb after them never changes.

lesson.heading: Other verbs: use do / does / did
lesson.text: For verbs like *want*, *work*, *play* and *have* we need **don't**, **doesn't** or **didn't**.

examples.note: positive: I want to go out.

examples.text: I **didn't get** up early this morning.
examples.note: positive: I got up early this morning.
positive: Diane had dinner with us.

lesson.heading: Don't look! and don't do
lesson.text: To tell somebody *not* to do something, we start with **Don't**. Sometimes **do** is the main verb, so we say **don't do**, **doesn't do**, **didn't do**.
After don't / doesn't / didn't the verb never changes: *she doesn't play*, not ~~she doesn't plays~~.

exercises.prompt: They aren't rich. They ___ got much money.
*A:* Would you like something to eat? *B:* No, thank you. I ___ hungry.
exercises.explanation: The negative of I am is I'm not.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginning of each negative sentence with its ending.
I ___ find my glasses. Have you seen them?
exercises.explanation: The negative of can is can't (cannot).

exercises.prompt: Steve ___ use email much. He prefers to talk on the phone.
exercises.explanation: use is a normal verb and Steve = he, so we need doesn't.

exercises.prompt: It rained yesterday. Now make it negative: It ___ yesterday.
exercises.explanation: After didn't the verb has no ending: didn't rain.
To tell somebody not to do something we start with Don't.

exercises.prompt: Which negative word goes in each sentence: don't, doesn't or didn't?
I've been to Japan many times, but I ___ been to Korea.

exercises.statement: We didn't see what happened. We weren't looking at the time.
exercises.explanation: Correct. weren't = were not, the negative of were.

exercises.prompt: You ask Gary: 'Were you born in London?' He answers 'No.' Put the words in order to write about Gary.
exercises.explanation: The negative of was is wasn't.

exercises.prompt: You ___ drive so fast. It's dangerous.
exercises.explanation: shouldn't (or mustn't) tells somebody that something is a bad idea.
